title: KV shadowing & speculative compactness estimator + prefill orchestrator
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Fragmentation of paged KV storage and imprecise admission of prefill work cause wasted decode cycles and unexpected tail latency. Current eviction heuristics operate after pressure events and cannot anticipate fragment coalescing opportunities or transient adjacency across slots. This ticket proposes a two-part system: 1) a lightweight KV shadowing layer that opportunistically tracks slot adjacency and access footprints without materializing extra pinned memory; 2) a speculative compactness estimator that assigns a compactness score to fragments to guide prefill admission, kernel selection, and cooperative compaction scheduling.
goal: Reduce end-to-end prefill-induced tail latency and wasted decode work by making prefill admission and background compaction fragment-aware. Improve token-cost efficiency of paged-attention workloads while keeping average latency within current SLOs.
design_decisions: Shadowing is read-only metadata kept in a probabilistic vector per shard to limit memory overhead (bloom-like), updated on decode/prefill events.
Compactness estimator uses short-term access recency + adjacency score + fragment size to compute a single 0..1 score.
Admission controller uses compactness score + current decode queue depth to accept/speculatively delay prefill jobs; accepted prefill jobs are tagged for kernel affinity hints.
Avoid long synchronous compaction during critical-path decodes; schedule background micro-compacts during idle windows or completed minibatches.
Expose a tunable knob for conservative/aggressive compacting to Dedicated customers via console.
Telemetry hooks: emit fragment score distributions and prefill acceptance rates to Console for regression detection.
Keep kernel routing decisions compatible with existing kernel selector: compactness score provides hints but final kernel selection is local and validated by runtime constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side simulation shows >= 12% reduction in wasted prefill decode token count on our heavy-concat benchmark (95th percentile workloads).
95th percentile tail latency for prefill-triggered requests should not increase by more than 5% compared to baseline on throughput tests.
Feature gated behind runtime flag with safe default (disabled in Private by default).
Unit + integration tests for shadow metadata update semantics and estimator determinism added to runtime-test suite.
Performance dashboard showing fragment score histogram, prefill accept/delay ratio, and compaction time per shard.
Design doc and implementation PR reviewed by runtime and serving infra leads.

implementation_notes: Shadowing structure must be lock-free on hot path: use per-worker local buffers and periodic fold into shard-level vector to avoid contention.
Compactness score should be cheaply computable (<= 10ns per fragment) to be feasible at admission time.
Admission controller should degrade to original behavior if shard metadata is stale or unavailable.
Micro-compaction must respect tenant isolation and correctness — verify with reproducers that compaction preserves KV lookup semantics.
Add A/B experiment flags to evaluate conservative vs aggressive modes on a subset of Dedicated hosts before global rollout.
metrics: Prefill_accept_rate_by_score_bucket: observe decreasing accept rates for low-score buckets
Compaction_cpu_ms_per_shard: keep under 2ms average during background windows
test_plan: Unit tests for shadow fold/freshness semantics
Deterministic simulation run against recorded production trace (7 day) to measure token savings
Load test with synthetic mixed-sequence distribution to measure tail latency
Chaos test: kill micro-compact worker and validate graceful fallback
Cross-tenant fairness test to ensure admission doesn't starve small tenants
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind runtime config; default off in Private and Dedicated initial rollout
Enable on 5% of Hosted hosts in Canary pool for 48h; monitor metrics and alarms
Expand to 25% for one week; run cost/latency regression checks
Enable conservative mode by default for remaining hosts; allow opt-in aggressive mode via Console
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window with daily anomaly review
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shadow metadata becomes stale and causes unnecessary prefill delays. Mitigation: fallback path accepts prefill after timeout and emit metric for staleness.
Risk: Micro-compaction competes with decode for GPU/CPU. Mitigation: soft-preempt and schedule only during known idle windows; throttle worker by host load.
Risk: Kernel hints cause suboptimal kernel selection. Mitigation: hints are advisory; measure kernel switch regressions and revert hints if harm observed.
Risk: Memory overhead for shadow vectors at high shard counts. Mitigation: use probabilistic structures, cap per-shard budget, evict oldest shadow entries.
Risk: Complexity increases maintenance burden. Mitigation: keep public interfaces small and document behavior clearly.
